content.thinking: क्री is ubhayapadi, so both pada forms work for the first-person plural benedictive - parasmaipada gives क्रीयास्म, atmanepada gives क्रेषीमहि. I'll go with the parasmaipada form, क्रीयास्म.

I'm working out the root हुर्छ् as parasmaipada, seṭ, forming लृट् as हुर्छिष्यन्ति—checking whether the penultimate letter र् triggers guṇa, and it doesn't since guṇa applies to vowels, not consonants, so I'm considering if rule 8.2.78 "upadhāyāṃ ca" applies here instead.

Actually, that rule lengthens the preceding ik vowel when the upadha is r or v followed by a hal, giving हूर्छति, so the future form should be हूर्छिष्यन्ति.

I'm checking the accent marker on the root eṣ — it's anudātta, so this takes ātmanepada endings for third person dual. Since eṣ begins with a long guru vowel, the rule for ijādi guru roots applies, triggering the āṭ augment before the ending.

Then combining with kṛ (which follows āmpratyaya as ātmanepadi), the third dual ātmanepada form comes out as एषाञ्चक्राते — I'm ruling out alternatives using as/bhū since those take parasmaipada forms instead.

I'm checking whether पुथ (divādi, meaning हिंसा) falls under the puṣādi group, since that determines whether it takes parasmaipada by the sutra 3.1.55 for the aorist formation.

Recalling the divādi roots list, I find कुथ, पुथ, गुध, क्षिप, पुष्प following the earlier sequence of पुष, शुष, दुष, श्लिष etc. — this confirms पुथ is indeed within puṣādi, so the aorist should be अपुथत् for third person and the same for second person plural.
This root कृञ् is ubhayapada due to ञित्, so uttama dual in liṭ gives चकृव (parasmaipada) and चकृवहे (atmanepada). Since kṛ is aniṭ, the क्रादिनियम sutra confirms no iṭ augment applies here in liṭ.

I'm working through the root रघ् with णिच् causative formation — the इदित् marker triggers नुम् insertion giving रङ्घयति, and I'm now checking whether the लृङ् form takes आत्मनेपद or परस्मैपद based on the णिच् conditioning rules.

Actually, I should double-check whether रघ carries इदित् at all — the ँ on the final vowel might just mark anunasika अ as इत्, not an इदित् root, which would mean no नुम् insertion and a different classification altogether, possibly as an अदन्त root in the curadi list where अतो लोपः applies.

So रघ् being non-adanta means राघयति, with lṛṅ 2sg giving अराघयिष्यः. I'm trying to recall whether Madhaviya Dhatuvritti treats रघ similarly to लघ as an alternate reading.

I'm checking whether this root falls under the pushādi subgroup within divadi, which would trigger aṅ in luṅ for parasmaipada forms—that pushādi group spans from puṣ through the end of the divadi class.

Looking at the actual dhātupātha sequence, I find knas listed just before pushādi begins, among roots like ṣṭhiv, ṣṇu, ṣṇas, vyuṣ, pluṣ, and others. Since knas takes iṭ in luṅ, it forms sic-luṅ with the sūtra 7.2.7 giving optional vṛddhi before a hal-ādi iṭ, yielding both aknasīt and aknāsīt as valid forms.

The root स्तु is ubhayapadi but being ञित् marked. For लुङ् in parasmaipada, the rule 7.2.72 grants iट् to sic for these specific roots, giving the form अस्तावीत्.

Applying vriddhi (7.2.1) for the sic-pratyaya in parasmaipada, I get the full set: अस्तावीत्, अस्ताविष्टाम्, अस्ताविषुः for third person, and the 2nd person plural ends up as अस्ताविष्ट — checking that no ष-त्व conditioning applies here since there's no upasarga to trigger 8.3.63.

I'm checking the root विद् (rudhādi, "to consider") - its accent marking shows anudātta, confirming it's ātmanepada and aniṭ, conjugating as विन्ते, विन्दाते, विन्दते. Now I'm working out the luṅ ātmanepada forms from this.

For aniṭ sic-luṅ with a consonant-final root and ik-upadhā, the kit-designation from the sūtra blocks guṇa, and the s gets deleted before jh/jhal, giving अविद्+त → अवित्त through the jhalo jhali rule.

I'm recalling the root चमु (cam), which belongs to the svadi class meaning "to eat" (भक्षण), trying to place it correctly among the other roots listed in that group.

For the liṭ madhyama dual parasmaipada form, the ending is "athuḥ". Since the abhyāsa (reduplicate) च is identical to the original and the rule about single consonants without substitution applies, I get चेमथुः as the final form.

I'm recalling that this root belongs to the tanadi class of the Dhatupatha, grouping it alongside similar roots like तनु, षणु, क्षणु, and तृणु, with घृणु specifically meaning "to shine."

Since the svarita marking makes it ubhayapadi, I'm working out the parasmaipada form for the vidhiliṅ dual uttama. I'm checking whether the lopa rule for the u-vikaraṇa before m/v applies here, concluding it doesn't since yāsuṭ intervenes, which should give घृणुयाव — but then I'm second-guessing whether guṇa of the root vowel should also apply given the laghūpadha rule, since the established form घृणोति shows no such change.

I'm piecing together the Siddhanta Kaumudi forms for these tanadi roots: तृणु gives तर्णोति/तर्णुते, घृणु gives घर्णोति/घर्णुते, and क्षिणु gives क्षेणोति with the guna applying due to the ardhadhatuka u-pratyaya condition.

For the vidhilin of घृणु, I'm settling on घर्णुयात्, घर्णुयाताम्, with the dual-we form घर्णुयाव.
For हा (to abandon, class 3 parasmaipada), the second person dual present is जहिथः or जहीथः, with rule 6.4.116 allowing the optional lengthening—I'll go with जहीथः.

Working through धन् in laṅ lakāra: reduplication gives dadhan, and after adding the tense marker, the saṃyogānta/halṅyādi lopa rules drop the final त्, yielding अदधन् for third person singular. Let me verify this against the Siddhanta Kaumudi reference.
I'm checking that पिष् is class 7 parasmaipada and aniṭ, so the 3rd person dual perfect would be पिपिषतुः.

I'm working through प्री (prītau), checking whether it's ātmanepada and anit, and tracing how the s-aorist (luṅ) forms via sic, considering whether sūtra 1.2.11 governing ātmanepada with sic applies here given the root's ik-ending.

I'm testing this against similar ik-ending roots like कृ, दी, ची, and नी to see if sic takes kit designation (blocking guṇa) consistently, comparing forms like अकृथाः, अदीष्ट, अचेष्ट, and अनेष्ट to resolve the inconsistency I'm noticing in guṇa application.

For प्री specifically, following the seṭ pattern of डीङ् → अडयिष्ट, I'm deriving अप्रेष्ठाः: सिच् + थास् combining to अप्रेस्थाः, then applying ṣatva to get अप्रेष्थाः, and finally ṣṭutva to arrive at the final form अप्रेष्ठाः.

I'm working out कॄत् with णिच् in curadi: the उपधायाश्च rule turns the ऋ into इर्, giving कीर्तयति, and I'm checking whether this root takes ubhayapada forms.

Since it's parasmaipada here, for first person singular vidhiliṅ the form becomes कीर्तयेयम्.

I'm checking the root गा (stutau) in the juhotyādi class, parasmaipada, trying to work out its reduplicated form जिगाति and which grammatical rule governs the reduplication for this root.

For the second person plural laṅ, I'm applying rule 6.4.113 (ई हल्यघोः), which replaces the weak stem's आ with ई before a hal-initial sārvadhātuka ending in abhyasta roots, giving forms like जिगीतः and जिगति, and building out the full laṅ paradigm to arrive at अजिगीत for 2nd person plural.

For root yujir, being ubhayapadi with luṅ, the irit status allows aṅ formation in parasmaipada too, so I can get ayujāma alongside the vṛddhi form ayaukṣma, with ātmanepada giving ayukṣmahi — I'll go with अयुजाम as the first person plural form.
For रु in liṭ, third plural needs reduplicated form ruru plus the kit ending us, but since guṇa is blocked here, the uvaṅ substitution rule for roots like ru applies, giving रुरुवुः.

The root वास (curadi, "to dwell/reside") forms वासयति in causative, with lut future वासयिता. Since curadi roots with the णिच् causative marker are typically ubhayapadi, I can give either पद form for madhyama purusha bahuvachana — परस्मैपद वासयितास्थ or आत्मनेपद वासयिताध्वे. I'll settle on वासयितास्थ.
For धिष् (class 3, parasmaipada) in lan, dual, I reduplicate to दिधिष्, then with the weak तास् ending (apit, no guna) and षत्व conversion of ष्+त to ष्ट, I get अदिधिष्टाम्.
For पुष् (to nourish), I'm working out the optative parasmaipada forms: पुष्णीयात् for third person singular, पुष्णीयाताम् for dual, and पुष्णीयुः for plural.
For नॄ (class 9, parasmaipada), the ashirlin active 3sg forms as नीर्यात् through the same ॠत→इर् guna process as कॄ→कीर्यात् and तॄ→तीर्यात्.
I'm working through the root भञ्ज् (bhañj) to confirm its luṅ (aorist) form uses the sic aorist with vṛddhi, giving अभाङ्क्षीत् as the standard result.

The root शुल्क (curadi class) takes णिच्, giving शुल्कयति, and since curadi roots are generally ubhayapadi, the Lut 3rd person singular form works out to शुल्कयिता for both parasmaipada and atmanepada.

I'm trying to recall the exact root "aha~" in the svadi class and its meaning of vyāptau (pervading), cross-checking it against other svadi roots like tik, tig, ṣagh, and dhṛṣ to pin down the correct form.

For the lit 3rd singular parasmaipada, I'm working through the derivation: dvitva doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, and ata ādeḥ vṛddhi to get from "ah" to "āha". The final answer is आह.

I'm trying to recall the exact root in the Svadi gana list—tig meaning āskandana (leaping/going)—and checking whether the anunasika marker on it signals parasmaipada rather than ātmanepada conjugation.

For the lit (perfect) 3rd person dual, I'm building tig → titig + atus, and since atus is a kit affix here (asamyogāl liṭ kit), there's no guna strengthening, giving titigatuḥ.

I'm working through the benedictive (ashirlin) form of root शॄ, applying the sutra that converts ॠ to इर् for such roots, then the lengthening rule under हलि च, arriving at a form like शीर्यात् by analogy with कीर्यात् and गीर्यात्.

The first person dual benedictive form would then be शीर्यास्व.

I'm considering मीङ् (divadi, आत्मनेपदी) and whether sutra 6.1.50, which substitutes आ for roots like मी/मिनु/दीङ् before ल्यप् when guna would otherwise arise, actually applies to this particular root in the lun form.

I'm working through the लुन् for मीङ् — checking if it takes सिच् as कित् in आत्मनेपद per 1.2.11, which would give अमेष्ट, अमेषाताम्, अमेषत without guna.

I'm working through the root ghṛ, class 3, anudātta anit parasmaipada verb, tracing how reduplication applies via the kuhoścuḥ and carcca rules to get the abhyāsa form, and checking whether the special ṛ/pṛ reduplication rule (7.4.77) gives jighṛ instead.

Recalling the Siddhanta Kaumudi forms for ghṛ: jagharti, jaghṛtaḥ, jaghrati, jaghāra, jaghartha, and the future/other derivatives like ghartā and gharishyati, trying to confirm whether the reduplication vowel is i or a.

I'm trying to recall the exact root in curadi gana, scanning through candidates like "स्तेन", "पद", "गृह", "मृग", "कुह", "शूर" to find the one matching the meaning I need.

Either way, treating it as curadi root "अस्त्" with णिच् gives अस्ति, and since the उपध is स् rather than अ, there's no vृद्धि needed, so the Lut form comes out as अस्तयिता.

I'm working out the āśīrliṅ ātmanepada form for root दृ (to respect), tudādi class, which is aniṭ since it's anudātta-marked. Forming the 3rd person dual sīyāstām, I'm checking whether rules like "ṛtaś ca saṃyogādeḥ" for iṭ augmentation apply here, and considering sutra 1.2.12 "uśca" regarding liṅ.

Since the sic-ātmanepada ending after an ṛ-ending root is kit, there's no guṇa applied, giving दृषीयास्ताम् (parallel to कृषीयास्ताम् from कृ). I'm confirming the 6.4 rule for riṅ before yak/yādi forms doesn't apply since sīyāstām starts with स, not य, so दृषीयास्ताम् stands as the correct form.

I'm trying to recall whether कुट् belongs to the curadi class and checking what form it would take with णिच् — considering laghūpadha guṇa giving कोटि, but I'm unsure if this root actually appears in curadi with that meaning.

For the Lut passive, I'm working through the चिण्वद्भाव rule that applies to णिजन्त roots, which allows either णि-lopa or retention, giving alternate forms like कारिता/कारयिता or भाविता/भावयिता as parallel examples. So I conclude the simplest third-person plural Lut form would be कोटयितारः.

I'm working through the root masj in luṅ (aorist), applying sic and the relevant sutras to derive forms like amāṅkṣīt, amāṅktām, amāṅkṣuḥ, checking the vṛddhi conditioning before the nasal-final root.

I'm checking the root kās — the anudātta mark on the ṛ indicates it's an ātmanepadī verb, so it conjugates as kāsate. I'm also considering whether there's a vārttika exception affecting this since it starts with k rather than a vowel.

By the rule "kāsprayayādām amantre liṭi" (3.1.35), kās takes ām in liṭ, giving kāsāñcakre. For second person singular ātmanepada, since the root itself is ātmanepadī (unlike bhū and as which are parasmaipada), I arrive at kāsāñcakṛṣe.

I'm trying to locate this root's correct classification — checking whether it belongs to tudādi with ātmanepada or rudhādi with parasmaipada, since "ओविजी भयचलनयोः" appears to exist in both gaṇas with different pada assignments.

For the liṭ uttama dual form, I need to work through whether vij is seṭ and how the iṭ augment behaves — since 1.2.2 makes iṭ after vij function as ṅit (blocking guṇa), and vas is already apit/kit in liṭ anyway, the resulting form comes out as विविजिव.

I'm tracing the root स्फुर्छ् from the Dhatupatha, noting it's seṭ and parasmaipada, and working through how the उपधायां च rule (8.2.78) would lengthen the penultimate vowel before र्/व् followed by a consonant.

Applying this to स्फुर्छ्, the preceding उ lengthens before र् since it's followed by the consonant छ्, giving स्फूर्छति (like मूर्छति, हूर्छति). For the lṛṅ form, the same lengthening rule carries through, so the answer comes out to अस्फूर्छिष्याव.

I'm checking the juhotyādi root पॄ meaning "to protect/fill," noting it's listed with short ṛ here though Siddhanta Kaumudi gives it as long ṝ, and recalling its forms like पिपर्ति, पिपूर्तः, पिपुरति.

I'm tracing the root जस् (हिंसायाम्, curadi class) through its causative formation जासि/जास्, and considering whether चिण्वद्भाव rules apply optionally when forming the passive of lut with the णिच् affix present.

Comparing with standard examples like भाविता/भावयिता and कारिता/कारयिता, I conclude both जासिता/जासयिता and जासितारौ/जासयितारौ are valid dual forms, settling on जासयितारौ as the general choice matching the active voice pattern.

The root ष्टीमँ reduces to stīm through ṣatva and ṣṭutva reversal rules, placed in divādi gaṇa, parasmaipada, meaning "to be wet" — and it's a seṭ root for luṅ formation.

Working through the iṭ aorist: since the vowel ī is long (not igantaḥ), the vṛddhi rule for sic doesn't apply the same way, and neṭi blocks vṛddhi for seṭ roots anyway, giving अस्तीमीत् with aḍāgama plus iṭ plus sic plus the iṭ-sandhi.

I'm confirming ग्रन्थ् is a class 9 parasmaipada root where the nasal drops before श्ना due to being anidit, giving ग्रथ्नाति, with optative forms ग्रथ्नीयात् — checking the Dhatupatha listing to verify it's parasmaipada rather than ubhayapada.

I'm trying to parse the root ञितृषाँ, meaning "to thirst," from the Dhatupatha's fourth class parasmaipada list, and puzzling over what the nasalized ā marker at the end signifies here.

Tracing through, tṛṣ falls under the puṣādi group within divādi verbs — a gaṇa spanning from puṣ to the end of the fourth class — which means it takes the aṅ augment in luṅ for parasmaipada forms.

Since aṅ is ṅit, no guṇa occurs, and being a seṭ root gives the dual form अतृषाव.

I'm trying to recall the exact Dhatupatha entry for the root गुर्द, checking whether it belongs to the curadi class with the meaning "पूर्वनिकेतने," and cross-referencing it against similar curadi roots to pin down its correct classification.

Still scanning through the curadi root list for गुर्द, moving past unrelated entries like चपि, क्षपि, छजि, श्वर्त, यम, चह, रह, बल, चिञ्, घट्ट, मुस्त, खट्ट, and others without finding it yet.

Continuing through the curadi list—गुर्द, जसि, ईड, जसु, पिडि, रुष, डिप, ष्टुप—these are parasmaipadi by default though technically ubhayapadi via णिच्. I'm working out the लङ् मध्यम एकवचन form for गुर्दयति, checking whether the उपधा र requires गुण.

Since the र् conjunct blocks the u from counting as laghu, no guna applies here, so the form stays अगुर्दयः.

I'm trying to locate the root त्रुट् in the Dhatupatha's curadi class, checking whether it's listed as "त्रुटँ छेदने" and whether it takes ātmanepada endings there, though this detail doesn't actually affect the passive form I'm deriving.

Working through the णिच् addition giving त्रोटि, then tracing how the Lut passive formation interacts with the ciṇvadbhāva rule for ajanta roots—specifically whether णि-lopa applies given the seṭ status of the तास् suffix, comparing it to the known kārayitā/kārita pattern for other णिजन्त roots.

So the two valid forms for third person singular Lut passive are त्रोटयिता and त्रोटिता. For second person dual ātmanepada, the answer is त्रोटयितासाथे.

I'm working through the root खण्ड् (curadi class, खण्डयति) to derive the optative passive first-person plural form खण्डयिषीमहि, applying iṭ-āgama and the ātmanepada uttama bahuvacana ending -सीमहि, while also considering the chinvadbhāva rule governing bhāva-karmaṇi derivations.

I'm checking the Dhatupatha entry for बध् (bandhane) in the bhvādi class, noting the anudātta accent marking it as an aniṭ root similar to गुप्, तिज्, and मान्.

This group of roots is anudāttet, making them ātmanepadī, and the anudātta it-marker on मान् signals the same pattern. Sutras 3.1.6 and the related vārttikas show these roots take sanādi affixes in svārtha senses—specifically बध् in the meaning चित्तविकार (disgust) takes san, giving बीभत्सते with reduplication per the dīrgha rule. Working out luṅ for this san-derived stem: since बीभत्स has multiple vowels, it's seṭ, producing अबीभत्सिषि, अबीभत्सिष्वहि, अबीभत्सिष्महि in ātmanepada.

The third person singular would be अबीभत्सिष्ट, and the first-person dual remains अबीभत्सिष्वहि — this matches the expected convention of deriving through san rather than the simple root, so अबीभत्सिष्वहि stands as the answer.

I'm working through the kryadi root मृड् (class 9, meaning to crush/be happy), checking its present tense मृड्णाति and deriving the vidhilin form मृड्णीयात् through श्ना affixation with यासुट् and the ई substitution, then applying ष्टुना ष्टुः to convert न to ण after ड्.

I'm examining the root दृ (svadi class, meaning हिंसा/to harm), checking whether it's parasmaipada and aniṭ based on the accent marking, then working out its liṭ third-person plural form, comparing it with how ṝ-ending roots like दॄ behave in that formation.

Since दृ isn't saṃyogādi (doesn't start with a conjunct), the yaṇ substitution applies rather than guṇa, giving दद्रुः — similar to how कृ becomes चक्रुः.

I'm looking at the root उब्ज (ujj, "to be straight/crooked"), tudādi class, parasmaipada — noting the grammatical dispute over whether the penultimate letter is ब or द, since commentators differ on this point when forming words like उदुब्जित.

Since उब्ज् is guru-mat (beginning with a guru vowel before a conjunct), it takes आम् in perfect tense, giving उब्जाञ्चकार (or alternately उब्जाम्बभूव, उब्जामास) — I'll settle on उब्जाञ्चकार as the answer.
For वृ (to choose), a kryādi ṅit ātmanepada root, the thās ending becomes sva, giving वृणीष्व with the natural षत्व change after ई.

I'm working through the root ci's lit forms, noting it's ubhayapadi and could form either परस्मैपद or आत्मनेपद, and examining the optional कुत्व rule in लिट् as well as whether इट् augment applies given ci's anit status.

Checking the derivation with यण् sandhi for forms with iṭ augment, I verify that uttama bahuvacana gives चिच्यिम and चिक्यिम (atmanepada चिच्यिमहे/चिक्यिमहे), confirming via comparison with standard forms like चिचाय, चिच्यतुः, चिच्युः and the analogous नी root giving निन्यिम.

I'm tracing the root तञ्चू (tañc) in the rudhādi class—it takes the śnam infix, then nalopa by 6.4.23 drops the nasal, giving forms like तनक्ति for third person singular present.

content.thinking: I'm working through the causative of ब्रू in the āśīrliṅ ātmanepada 2sg, adding the ṇic and seṭ iṭ to form ब्रूसयिषीष्ठाः, and noting that the karmaṇi construction could optionally take the ciṇvad treatment.

I'm tracing this root to the tudādi class, ātmanepadī — लज्जते, "to be ashamed," confirming it's ओलज्जी व्रीडायाम् rather than ओविजी भयचलनयोः.

For the aorist (luṅ) ātmanepada first person dual, since the root is seṭ, the form works out to अलज्जिष्वहि.

I'm working out that व्रीड् being divādi and parasmaipada with seṭ takes the iṭ-aorist, giving forms like अव्रीडिषम्. I'm also checking whether vrīḍ falls under the puṣādi group within divādi, which would instead trigger the aṅ-aorist per 3.1.55.

Continuing through the rest of puṣādi's list, I find vrīḍa actually belongs to divādi's earlier portion alongside iṣa, ṣaha, ṣuha, jṛṣ, jhṛṣ — so its iṭ aorist would be अव्रीडिष्म.

I'm tracing the root त्रुट् through curadi gaṇa, noting it takes ātmanepada and forms त्रोटि with guṇa, then working out how the passive/āśīrliṅ construction would apply to it.

Since णिजन्त roots end in a vowel, चिण्वद्भाव can optionally apply, deleting the णि. That gives two valid forms for the desiderative benedictive: त्रोटिषीष्ठाः (with चिण्वद्भाव) or त्रोटयिषीष्ठाः (without it).

I'm working out the root छृद् in the rudhādi class, meaning "to shine" (दीप्तिदेवनयोः), checking its ubhayapadi conjugation with श्नम् insertion, and deriving the first-person plural imperative form छृणदाम।

With आडुत्तमस्य पिच्च, the uttama endings become pit, giving the strong atmanepada form छृणदामहै (comparing with रुध् → रुणधामहै). Checking ṇatva, ऋ followed by न shifts to ण, confirming छृणत्ति and the imperative छृणदाम।

I'm checking the root ūrja in the curādi class, meaning "strength, nourishment." Since the upadhā letter is r rather than a vowel, there's no guṇa substitution, so the causative form should come out as ūrjayati, though I'm considering whether the short-u variant urjayati might also apply.

Different Dhatupatha editions vary between ऊर्ज and उर्ज for this root, but since the question explicitly gives उर्जँ, I'll stay consistent with that reading and go with उर्जयसि as the answer.

For the 9th class root अश् (भोजने), parasmaipada, I'm working out the third person plural perfect form: reduplication gives आशुः, since the नुट् augment from अश्नोतेश्च only applies to the 5th class आत्मनेपद root अशू (व्याप्तौ), not this one.

Grah is marked ubhayapada due to the svarita accent, so both parasmaipada and ātmanepada perfect forms are valid - जगृहिव for uttama dual. I'm checking whether grah takes seT augment, since it forms गृहीत with the long vowel.

Since lit generally takes iT except for the specific roots excluded by the rule, grah takes it here. Applying samprasāraṇa (grah → gṛh in kit-marked lit forms), the correct form is जगृहिव.

I'm working out khid's root class and conjugation — it's aniṭ, parasmaipada, so for luṅ I need to apply vṛddhi with sic: akhaitsīt in third singular, then checking the dual form akhaittam by working through the sandhi of a-khid-s-tam.

I'm working through the perfect tense derivation for the root vraśc, checking whether samprasāraṇa applies per the grahi-jyā sūtra since this root falls under that special class requiring vowel substitution for the semivowel in liṭ forms.

Checking iṭ rules for ūdit roots in liṭ — krādiniyama makes iṭ obligatory except for kṛ, sṛ, bhṛ, vṛ, stu, dru, sru, śru, so vavraśc gets iṭ forms like vavraścitha, vavraṣṭha.

I'll settle on vavraściva as the safer form here.

I'm working out the causative form of the root jas (curādi, meaning "to injure") — applying upadhā vṛddhi to get jāsayati, then checking the luṭ passive construction with the optional ciṇvadbhāva rule for tāsi-forms in bhāva and karmaṇi usage.

content.thinking: I'm tracking down the root बृहि in the Curadi gana, noting it's इदित् so नुम् gets inserted giving बृंह्, then checking whether guṇa applies with णिच् given the anusvara in the penultimate position—working toward the causal form बृंहयति and its लुट् form बृंहयिता.

I'm working through the root चुट्ट् of the curādi class, meaning "to be free" - checking whether guṇa applies to the upadha vowel before forming the causative stem चुट्टय, and considering whether this root takes both parasmaipadī and ātmanepadī endings or just one.

Since चुट्ट doesn't belong to the special ātmanepadī-only curādi groups, it should be ubhayapadī, so for the active voice I'll use the parasmaipada form. That gives अचुट्टयिष्यत् as the second person plural in lṛṅ.

Since प्रीञ् is ubhayapadi (ञit), both padas are valid in kartari; for AshirLin madhyama purusha bahuvachana, parasmaipada gives प्रीयास्त while atmanepada would be प्रेषीढ्वम्, so I'll go with प्रीयास्त.

I'm tracing the root kil in curadi class with meaning kshepe (to throw), confirming it takes Nic and forms kelayati, and since curadi roots are ubhayapadi by default, I'm checking the parasmaipada lrt form kelayishyati for third person singular.

Final answer: केलयिष्यथ.

I'm working through the vidhilin form of कि (class 3, ज्ञाने), building the reduplicated stem चिकि and checking how it combines with the यास् suffix, comparing it to similar जुहोत्यादि roots like बिभी to figure out whether इ shifts before the suffix.

So the answer settles on चिकियाः as the second person singular optative parasmaipada form.

The root लिह् is ubhayapadi, so for kartari ashirlin prathama dvivachana, both parasmaipada (लिह्यास्ताम्) and atmanepada (लिक्षीयास्ताम्) forms are valid; I'll go with the parasmaipada form लिह्यास्ताम्.

I'm tracing नट in the curadi class, checking whether it takes णिच् to form नाटयति, and recalling the Siddhanta Kaumudi's note on this root's meaning as "avaspandana" (trembling/pulsating).

Since both parasmaipada and ātmanepada apply, the Lut third-person plural form works out to नाटयितारः in either pada, giving the final answer नाटयितारः.

I'm working out the desiderative formation of this ubhayapadi root, checking whether it takes parasmaipada or atmanepada forms and applying the u-augment with guna for the uttama purusha dual ending, considering whether the elision rule for the u-pratyaya before m/v applies here.

I'm recalling that in ārdhadhātuka contexts, चक्षिङ् gets replaced by ख्याञ् per the rule चक्षिङः ख्याञ्, and since ख्याञ् is ñit it forms ubhayapada. There's also a vārttika allowing an optional क्शाञ् substitute in certain cases.

For āśīrliṅ, since it's ārdhadhātuka, the base remains ख्या, giving parasmaipada forms like ख्यायात्, ख्यायास्ताम्. The rule वान्यस्य संयोगादेः applies to saṃyogādi ā-ending roots, allowing an optional ए substitution in kit ārdhadhātuka liṅ, so forms like ख्येयात् alongside ख्यायात् are valid, and for madhyama bahuvacana parasmaipada both ख्यायास्त and ख्येयास्त work, with ख्यासीध्वम् for ātmanepada. Since both pada options and both vowel grades are grammatically acceptable here, I'll settle on ख्यायास्त as the answer.
